results.question: My printer is not printing anything
results.answer: Based on Ticket ID: TKT-031, the issue of the printer not printing could be due to the print spooler on the print server hanging, which can cause print jobs to sit in the queue with an 'Error' status. The resolution involved clearing the stuck jobs, restarting the Print Spooler service, and confirming that a test page printed successfully. If you're experiencing similar issues, you may want to check the print spooler status.

results.question: I cannot access SAP after my account was locked
results.answer:
To unlock your SAP account, it was confirmed that accounts can be auto-locked by the dormancy policy after 90 days of inactivity. In a similar case (Ticket ID: TKT-048), the account was reactivated in SU01, and the user was required to log in and change their password to confirm access was restored. 

If your account is locked, you may need to have it reactivated and follow the necessary steps to regain access.

results.question: My laptop screen went black and won't turn on
results.answer: Based on Ticket ID: TKT-019, the resolution for a laptop that will not power on is to isolate the fault. In that case, the issue was determined to be a failed dock power adapter rather than the laptop itself. The recommended steps are to connect the laptop directly to a known-good charger, perform a battery-drain reset, and if necessary, replace the faulty power adapter. After these steps, the laptop should boot normally.

results.question: I need access to Power BI for my team
results.answer:
To grant Power BI access to your team, you can follow a similar process as outlined in Ticket ID: TKT-014. In that case, the analyst was assigned a Power BI Pro license in the Microsoft 365 admin center and added to the Finance workspace as a Viewer. Ensure that your team members have the appropriate licenses and are added to the necessary workspaces. 

If you need further assistance, please refer to Ticket ID: TKT-078, where a user regained access after a manual sync was performed due to a failed sync job. 

For more detailed steps, you may need to consult your IT department or the Microsoft 365 admin center.

results.question: Network drive is not showing up on my computer
results.answer:

The resolution indicated that the problem was related to UNC network shares. It suggests ensuring that the correct URL format is used when accessing network shares. 

If you are having trouble with a network drive, make sure you are using the correct path and that the share is properly configured.

results.question: I forgot my Windows password and am locked out
results.answer:
To reset a forgotten Windows password, you can verify your identity through a manager or employee ID, then reset the Active Directory password and clear any account lockout. After that, you can set a new password at the next logon. This process is similar to what was done in Ticket ID: TKT-007, where the user's identity was verified, and the password was reset. 

Ticket ID: TKT-007.

results.question: VPN disconnects every few minutes while working from home
results.answer: To fix frequent VPN disconnects while working from home, you can refer to Ticket ID: TKT-004. The resolution involved tracing the drops to an aggressive idle-timeout on the user's consumer router and a low DPD value in the group policy. The solution was to raise the dead-peer-detection interval on the VPN profile and advise disabling the router's Wi-Fi power-saving mode, which stabilized the session.

results.question: Printer shows offline but is turned on
results.answer: The printer is showing offline because it had picked up a new DHCP address while its print queue still pointed at the old IP. A DHCP reservation was set for the printer's MAC, the port on the print server was updated to the new address, and it was confirmed that the queue came back online for all users. This information is based on Ticket ID: TKT-036.

results.question: Computer is running very slowly after Windows update
results.answer:
To fix slow computer performance after a Windows update, you can refer to Ticket ID: TKT-095. The resolution involved rolling back a broken generic Bluetooth driver that was causing issues across the office fleet. While this specific ticket addresses Bluetooth issues, it highlights the importance of checking for driver-related problems after an update. 

For general slow performance, you might also consider checking for full storage or thermal issues, as seen in Ticket ID: TKT-022, where diagnostics showed the SSD was 98% full and there was thermal throttling due to dust-clogged vents. In that case, clearing temp files, offloading data, and cleaning the vents resolved the performance issues.

If you need more specific steps, please refer to the relevant tickets.

results.question: Cannot install Adobe Acrobat on my work laptop
results.answer:
Based on Ticket ID: TKT-151, the issue of being unable to install an application on a work laptop is addressed. The resolution involved confirming that the laptop was under a standard-user policy that blocks local-admin installs. Instead of granting standing admin rights, the approved application package was pushed through the Company Portal / Software Center, allowing it to install under the system account. 

If you are facing a similar issue with Adobe Acrobat, you may need to follow a similar process.

results.question: WiFi keeps dropping in the conference room
results.answer:
The issue of WiFi dropping in the conference room may be related to network coverage or interference. In a similar case (Ticket ID: TKT-132), access points across a building were found to intermittently reboot due to a firmware update, causing drops for connected users. The resolution involved rolling back the firmware and applying a patch to stabilize the connection. 

For your specific situation, it may be beneficial to conduct a site survey to check for coverage and interference issues in the conference room. 

Please refer to Ticket ID: TKT-132 for more details on the resolution process.

results.question: Account locked after too many wrong password attempts
results.answer:
To unlock your account after multiple incorrect password attempts, you can follow the resolution from Ticket ID: TKT-067. In that case, the user's identity was verified in person, and they were walked to the badge office to reissue a working smart card. Additionally, the PIN counter was reset, and the new card was re-enrolled to their account, which confirmed successful login. 

If you are unable to verify your identity in person, please contact your IT support for further assistance.

results.question: AnyConnect shows login failed after password reset
results.answer:
Based on Ticket ID: TKT-001, the resolution for a similar issue states that the user's Active Directory account was locked due to repeated failed MFA prompts. The account was unlocked in AD, the Duo MFA device pairing was reset, and it was confirmed that AnyConnect connected successfully to the GR-VPN gateway. 

If you are experiencing a login failure after a password reset, it may be worth checking if your account is locked or if there are issues with MFA.
